title: How much of an open-source chip design search can cheap fidelity rungs and proof prediction save, with a guarantee?
lede: milestones 1 to 3 done: on 10 designs x 60 ABC pass sequences, the generic-gate score does not rank like routed SKY130 area x delay (tau-b median -0.04), and liberty mapping mis-ranks too when the clock is tight (tau 0.59); at equal wall-clock a one-shot cheap-rung screen does not beat random or hill-climbing search on the cached table; successive halving across rungs does not beat random routed search on mean regret either (plain halving from the generic-gate rung is worst; a 6-point routed pilot to pick the start rung fixes most of that, H3), a 10-point routed pilot plus a conformal bound on the mapped rung keeps the routed optimum 0.99 of the time (nominal 0.90) at 42 to 57% of the routed runs, but on the generic-gate rung coverage fails (0.65 against 0.80, H4 refuted there); proof-success prediction (H5): pooled AUC 0.96 to 0.998 across 15 designs is just design size (an oracle knowing only each design's success rate scores the same), and inside the one design with variation it is 0.65 to 0.78, so H5 is not supported; milestone 6 proves that halving's routed regret is at most the sum of the cut rungs' largest ranking inversions (vacuous for the generic-gate rung, loose for the mapped ones); milestone 7a adds a distribution-free pilot quantile of pair inversions (16-point pilots hold the nominal 0.8 coverage in all 60 group-rung cells, median 0.32 of the maximum), whose summed bound is under 0.1 on 9 of 10 groups for the mapped rungs at a relaxed clock but is violated by realised halving regret in 1 of 40 cells, so it is a heuristic, not a guarantee
summary: An open research programme; milestone 1 is measured. Over 10 small designs, 60 ABC pass sequences each and two clock targets (1,200 runs through Yosys, ABC and OpenROAD on SKY130 HD), the generic-gate rung's Kendall tau-b against routed (global-route plus timing repair) area × period is below 0.7 on all 9 designs where it is defined (median −0.04), and its pick costs a median 13.5% of routed area × period. The liberty-mapped rung is no better than 0.59 median tau at a tight clock (median regret 10.5%) but nearly exact at a relaxed one (0% regret), because timing repair reorders designs. Routed points cost about 8× a generic point here, so there is little to save on designs this small. Limits: one corner and utilisation, global-route estimates, ten small designs. Milestone 2 replays search on the cached table at equal wall-clock: screening the pool at the generic-gate or mapped rung and verifying the top points does not beat random or hill-climbing search (45 s: regret 1.08% and 1.27% against 0.94% and 0.61%), and loses badly at smaller budgets. Hypotheses H2 to H5 (multi-fidelity wins, coverage, proof prediction) are not yet run. Milestone 3 replays successive halving across the four rungs: starting from the generic-gate rung it is the worst strategy (about 10% mean routed regret at the tight clock at 45 s against 0.94% for random search); starting at the mapped rung wins on most designs at a relaxed clock but loses heavily on two; a 6-point routed pilot that picks the start rung recovers the designs plain halving loses (H3), so there is no multi-fidelity gain at equal wall-clock on this 50-point pool yet. Milestone 4 (H4) replays conformal shortlists: a routed pilot of 10 to 16 points calibrates a one-sided bound on routed area × delay from a cheap rung. On the mapped rung the routed optimum is kept 0.99 of the time at nominal 0.90 (0.90–0.92 at 0.80) while routing 42–57% of the pool, against 0.53–0.65 for random search with equal routed runs; on the generic-gate rung coverage is 0.65 at nominal 0.80, no better than random search, so H4 is refuted there. Limits: 20 groups from 10 small designs, one corner. H5 (milestone 5): across 752 Yosys SAT-miter proofs of ABC rewrites on 15 designs, proof time is set by design size (multiplier median 0.01 s at 4 bits, 11 s at 8, over 10 s at 9–10) and never by a rewrite failing; leave-one-design-out AUC is high pooled (0.96–0.998) only because it reads design size, and within the 8-bit multiplier it is 0.65–0.78 against 0.81 for the rule “the rewrite shrinks the netlist”. One solver, one timeout. Milestone 6 (theory): define a rung’s inversion as the largest log-factor by which it ranks a truly worse candidate at or ahead of a better one; halving’s routed regret is then at most the sum of the cut rungs’ inversions (proved; holds on all 40 table cells). It is vacuous for the generic-gate rung (inversion above 0.3 on 8 of 10 groups) and loose for the mapped rungs (bound 0.23–0.35 against about 0 realised); a 10-point pilot sees a median 52–67% of the inversion but cannot certify it. The probabilistic version is open.
